evidence.quote: We propose a substantial fund paid automatically, with fees separately stated
$30 million for the class, distributed automatically, plus $9 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses.
Fees were discussed in the opening round alongside the proposed class relief; they were not discussed only after class relief had been agreed.
a fee request that reflects the firm’s contingency investment
the $6 million fee would compensate the firm for its substantial investment.
Accepting secures a binding settlement that releases the overlapping claims and ends the litigation
Brightline accepts your latest term sheet as binding, subject to court approval.

summary: Plaintiffs first raised fees in their opening term sheets, and fees were negotiated alongside class relief before any class-only agreement was reached. Whitcombe Reyes’s private reasoning considered its own fee recovery, but the transcript does not clearly show counsel sacrificing class recovery for firm compensation or defense leveraging fees to reduce class relief. Defense accepted the lowest competing proposal from Whitcombe Reyes while noting it would release overlapping claims, supporting a reverse-auction-tactics label, but the court declaration accurately described the negotiation sequence.
